text:
Our Zanzibar trip was booked for 14 to 21 March through a travel agent in Kisumu, and the insurer's assessor wants a clear sequence of events before deciding the cancellation claim. I am the policyholder, Otieno Ochieng, policy TX-48213-K, and my wife Achieng Odhiambo is the second traveller. The agent we dealt with was Barasa Wekesa.

Two days before departure I was admitted overnight with a kidney stone, and the urologist told me not to fly for three weeks. He started me on tamsulosin 0.4 mg once daily and booked a repeat scan ten days later; my wife was not unwell and could have travelled alone.

The policy excess is KES 5,000 per claim. The hospital invoice came to KES 86,500, which I paid by card. The agent refunded the 12,000 shilling booking fee but kept the KES 45,000 deposit because the airline ticket was non-refundable.

You can reach me on 0712 555 0148 or otieno.o@example.invalid.

The airline gave me a 250 birr meal voucher and nothing for a hotel, because I slept at the airport on two chairs. I did not ask for a refund of the taxi fare. The duty manager at the gate, Kidist Abebe, wrote the delay times on a letter for me. Please confirm what I am owed and when it will be paid. My email is tigist.t@example.invalid.

My brother stayed with our mother that night, and I paid a neighbour 1,800 birr to sit with her until he arrived. She has advanced dementia and cannot be left alone after dark. He had to swap a night shift to do it, so I owe him a favour.

text:
On the second night of our Dubai trip I was taken to a clinic with a severe allergic reaction after a hotel dinner, and the doctor said it was probably peanuts although they never confirmed it. The treatment was an adrenaline injection and three hours on a drip, and the bill was AED 1,150, which I paid in cash and have a receipt for.

The suitcase failed to arrive on 12 October, and the airline's baggage desk gave me a property irregularity report numbered DXB-LX-55902 that I have not yet sent to anyone. The bag held two school-uniform dresses for my daughter, a laptop sleeve, a pair of leather sandals and my work files for the Kapsabet exams. I estimate the replacement value at about KES 62,000, but the laptop itself was in my hand luggage.

I am Chebet Koskei, a primary-school teacher, and my husband Kiprop Langat booked the trip on his card, although the policy TG-2061-M is in my name only. Please use chebet.k@example.invalid.

The airline moved my return flight twice, first to 18 September and then to 21 September, and the second change cost me a 7,500 shilling fee that the airline says is non-refundable. I kept the airline's emails showing both changes.

I paid 52,000 shillings for a new one-way ticket on a different airline, and the original return flight went unused. The hostel refunded the last five nights but kept the first night's deposit. Please call me on 0733 555 0194, and the claim is under the name Mwende Musyoka.

The reason I left early was my grandmother's death in Machakos, with the burial set for the 16th, so I flew on the 14th. I did not tell the airline why, and nobody there asked.

text: My connecting flight from Kisumu to Nairobi was cancelled at 16:30 on Tuesday, and the next seat the airline offered was on Thursday morning, which would have meant two nights in the city.
